segments.source: 1. X has more roads than Y. 2. Yet X has longer, not shorter, travel time. 3. Therefore the universal claim fails on this pair. Cross-domain check: 8×5=40 km.
Yes. X and Y form a counterexample. Cross-domain answer: 40 km.

Across several months, ice-cream sales and sunburn cases rise together. Temperature also rises in those months. No intervention is described. Cross-domain check: a survey team starts work at 12:00 and works for 2 hour(s) without a break.
Correlation between X and Y does not by itself prove X causes Y; a third variable may influence both. For the cross-domain check, finishing time = starting time + duration.
Can we conclude that ice-cream sales cause sunburn? Cross-domain check: at what time does the team finish?

1. Sales and sunburn are correlated. 2. Temperature is a plausible common factor stated in the data. 3. Without an intervention or stronger causal evidence, direct causation is not established. Cross-domain check: 12+2=14, so the team finishes at 14:00.
No. The association alone does not establish that ice-cream sales cause sunburn. Cross-domain answer: 14:00.

Two transport plans are compared. A costs 8, takes 20 minutes, and has safety score 9. B costs 10, takes 25 minutes, and has safety score 9. Lower cost/time and higher safety are better. Cross-domain check: a local committee has 11 members, requires at least 6 present for quorum, and 11 are present.
A Pareto-dominates B if A is at least as good on every stated criterion and strictly better on at least one. For the cross-domain check, quorum exists when present members ≥ the stated threshold.
Does one plan dominate the other? Cross-domain check: is quorum met?
1. A is cheaper than B. 2. A is faster than B. 3. Safety is equal. 4. A is no worse anywhere and better on two criteria. Cross-domain check: compare 11 with 6; 11≥6 is true.
A Pareto-dominates B. Cross-domain answer: quorum is met.

Part A — Foundational reasoning about the world
Problem 751. Position chain from Fern to Alder
A map can be modeled with relative positions. When several moves are given, their effects can be combined rather than memorized as a picture.
Meadow is 1 map unit(s) east of Fern; Alder is 1 map unit(s) east of Meadow. A museum in Meadow opens on Saturday.
Treat east as +x, west as −x, north as +y, and south as −y. Add the moves in order. A fact that does not affect any coordinate is irrelevant.
Where is Alder relative to Fern? What is the straight grid displacement measured as |x|+|y|? Identify any irrelevant fact.

1. Start Fern at (0,0). 2. Translate each relation into a coordinate move. 3. Adding the moves gives (2,0). 4. That coordinate is east of Fern; the grid displacement is |2|+|0|=2. 5. The museum sentence changes no coordinate, so it is a distractor.
Alder is east of Fern; grid displacement 2 unit(s). The museum fact is irrelevant.
Cardinal directions become easier to reason about when they are treated as relations that can be composed.
